standard_prerequisites.name: The injectivity of a module over a localization acted on invertibly
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source line 834)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the hull is injective as a module over the local ring at the prime.

core_obligations: Parts (2) and (3) first: the quotient into the residue field is an essential extension, so the uniqueness of injective hulls identifies the hull of the quotient with that of the residue field, and elements outside the prime act invertibly so that the hull is a module over the local ring, injective there by the cited statement (proof lines 825-834)

Indecomposability: a nonzero injective submodule meets the quotient in a nonzero submodule, and after shrinking may be assumed to be the injective hull of that intersection; since the quotient is an essential extension of the intersection, the inclusion of that hull into the ambient hull is an isomorphism, so no nontrivial decomposition exists (proof lines 835-842)
proof_roadmap: R/p ⊂ κ(p) 是本质扩张 ⇒ 由注入壳唯一性，(2) 成立。
f ∉ p 时 f: κ(p) → κ(p) 同构 ⇒ f: E → E 同构 ⇒ E 是 R_p-模；再由注入性引理 E 作为 R_p-模注入 ⇒ (3)。
若 0 ≠ E' ⊂ E 是注入子模，则 J = (R/p) ∩ E' ≠ 0；可缩小 E' 使其为 J 的注入壳；而 R/p 是 J 的本质扩张 ⇒ E' → E 是同构 ⇒ E 不可分解。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement says that for a prime p of a ring the injective hull of R/p is indecomposable, is the injective hull of the residue field, and is also the injective hull of the residue field over the local ring at p (author lemma at source lines 813-823, label lemma-injective-hull-indecomposable). The proof (source lines 825-843) uses the essentialness of R/p inside the residue field and the uniqueness of injective hulls for the second and third parts, the action of elements outside the prime to descend the module structure to the local ring, and shows indecomposability by intersecting an arbitrary nonzero injective submodule with R/p and upgrading the resulting inclusion of hulls to an isomorphism (proof lines 835-842). The indecomposability argument is the substance. H3.
